title: Signage types

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines

slide_intent: Adapt hierarchy to the navigational task so building, direction, room and floor information remain easy to distinguish.
strategic_value: A family of related sign types can give Helsinki visitors consistent cues at each stage of a journey.
demonstration: This expanded webpage-section capture presents main/floor directories, direction signs, room signs, icon signs and floor-number signs with diagrams and rule lists.
practical_value: Choose the sign type before composing its contents, then follow the corresponding alignment and spacing conditions.

content_islands.name: Main and floor directories
content_islands.spec: Begin with directory text, floor plan and grouped floor information examples.

content_islands.name: Directional and room signs
content_islands.spec: Compare arrows, words, languages and room labels through the middle sequence.

content_islands.name: Icon and floor signs
content_islands.spec: Finish with square pictogram and centered floor-number specimens.

ingredient.name: Wayfinding sign family
ingredient.role: Assign a consistent structure to each navigation task.
ingredient.application: Follow each sign type’s own arrangement: directional text opposite the arrow, separate text left-aligned, square icon/floor-number signs.
ingredient.scope: Building signage; room signs also permit centered alignment. Main/floor sign spacing references the logo protected area as a recommendation.

reference_purposes.Application: Five sign types are compared through detailed diagrams and instructions.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Direction text sits opposite its arrow; separated text aligns left; room signs may alternatively center; icon and floor-number signs use square formats.
